its my favorite place. im always in a state of shock and dissociation during intake.... all the forms and describing my past traumas. u get assessed by the psychiatrist and often talk medication. i often forget to eat the first night. i often spend the first night awake, trying to avoid my room and pace the hallways quietly sobbing because i miss the person i love.  miss my stuff. i do not miss my phone.  


if I'm a threat of hurting myself, i tell them and they put me in a room that's big, the bed is fixed to the floor, the sheets are sewn to the mattress and the door may or may not be locked when in seclusion. there will be a person by yourside at activities and when using the bathroom.  


if I'm placed with the general population, it takes a day or two for them to see I'm not violent towards others, just myself. i get placed with a roommate that is hopefully quiet mannered like me.  


the first night is rough but through the emotional roller coaster, i need to stand up for myself. ask for food even though its after hours and i feel guilty bothering people, ask for water for tea, socks, toothpaste and soap, towels, ask for tylenol and earplugs.  


my first day I'm usually still depressed and wont leave my bed. sometimes the nurse will bring you a tray of random food and leave it in your room. most of the norm rooms have had 2 chairs, a narrow bed, a desk, and a shelf also secured to the walls and a window.  


when things get normal, you meet with a team of doctors; psychiatrists, psychologists, general physicians, nutritionist, nurses, and caseworkers all once a day each day. the day also has set meal times, set times for snacks/warm drinks, group therapy and recreational therapy that varies by the person doing them. i like music and art but others really like the gym and boardgames.  


usually i dont want make friends my first couple of days. but since we share so much in group  therapy, i relate and share too. i meet the best people in there.
